name: Canada
tagline: Not one country to apply to, but five provinces with three routes
summary: Canada publishes plainly what it wants from an IB student: the points, the Higher Level subjects, the mathematics course that will not do. What it does not publish is a national anything. Education is provincial, so Ontario has a central application service, British Columbia has a different one, and Quebec, Alberta, Nova Scotia, Manitoba and Saskatchewan take you directly. The twenty universities on this page are spread across seven of those provinces, and picking Toronto and picking Vancouver puts a student on two different paths with different deadlines, different fees, different health cover and, in Quebec, a second immigration system on top of the federal one. The money is the other constraint: international undergraduate tuition runs past CAD 50,000 a year at UBC, though Saskatchewan charges CAD 39,007 for a BA in 2026/27 and Manitoba averages about CAD 28,000, and since 2024 the federal government caps how many study permit applications it will even look at.
whyConsider: Entry requirements are published as numbers. Universities state the IB points and the Higher Level subjects a programme needs, so you can tell in advance whether your predicted score is in range rather than guessing at a holistic process.
Offers come early and on predicted grades. UBC states plainly that it decides on interim grades and uses the July results only to confirm, which makes the IB calendar a condition rather than a cliff.
A bachelor's degree normally leads to a Post-Graduation Work Permit with no field-of-study restriction, which is a clearer route than US OPT.
Four-year degrees with co-op options at several universities, meaning paid work terms built into the degree. Waterloo built its reputation on this.
Both English and French are official languages, and Montreal in particular lets you study in English while living in French.
watchOuts: Do not read one Canadian deadline as Canada's. Toronto and UBC and McGill all close on 15 January 2027; Simon Fraser closes on 31 January, Concordia asks international applicants for 1 February (1 March for others), Alberta sets a date per programme, and Dalhousie closes its health programmes on 15 February and takes the rest as space allows. The province decides the route and the university decides the date.

The mathematics rule is decided two years before you apply. Toronto, UBC and McGill each refuse Mathematics: Applications and Interpretations SL for their science and business programmes. Dalhousie accepts it. Nothing after DP1 can repair that choice.

Bonus points are counted by some universities and not others. UBC's 24-point floor includes them; Toronto reads your total out of 42 with them excluded. The same predicted grades are three points apart depending on who is reading.

A study permit is not a formality. Undergraduates need a Provincial Attestation Letter to enter a capped queue, the 2026 cap was 309,670 applications nationally, and no allocation had been published for 2027 as of September 2026.

Quebec is a second immigration system. A Certificat d'acceptation du Quebec has its own fee, its own financial test and its own processing time, and it has to be granted before the federal permit can be.
Health cover is provincial and Ontario is the province where the answer is no. An international student there is outside the public plan for the whole degree and pays for UHIP instead.

No Ontario university on this page publishes a tuition figure for 2027/28. Toronto says its fees are set in the spring of the year of entry, so a student deciding in January is committing to a price that does not exist yet.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: No national minimum, because there is no national rule-owner to set one. Each university publishes its own and they do not agree: UBC requires 24 points including bonus points and says openly that most programmes need more; Dalhousie requires 26 including bonus points; Manitoba 24; York, Toronto Metropolitan, Carleton and Guelph 28; Toronto assesses on predicted or final results excluding bonus points, which is a different scale. Read the number off the university you actually want, and check whether it is out of 42 or 45.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Canadian universities normally require the full IB Diploma and then name prerequisite subjects for the programme. Toronto accepts prerequisites at Standard or Higher Level; UBC requires at least three Higher Level courses in the Diploma and assesses the subjects relevant to your intended field; McGill expects a 5 or better in every Higher and Standard Level subject for most programmes, which is a floor per subject rather than a total. The rule with the longest reach is mathematics: Toronto counts Mathematics: Applications and Interpretations SL towards Advanced Functions only, UBC excludes it from its science programmes, the Faculty of Management, Sauder and the Vancouver School of Economics, and McGill will not take it as a mathematics prerequisite at all. Dalhousie accepts it.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: There is no national conversion and no recognition body that publishes one. Each university maps IB grades onto its own admission average in its own way, and Ontario universities convert IB grades into percentage equivalents for comparison with Ontario's 4U courses. So there is no single table to use: read each university's own.
notes: Every route here decides on predicted results and confirms on final ones. UBC states it most clearly: initial decisions are made on interim grades reported by your school, and the final IB results confirm the decision and any first-year credit.

Final results normally have to reach the university electronically from the IBO. Toronto states that results issued by your school are not accepted in place of this, and requesting the transmission is your job.
Transfer credit for Higher Level subjects is common and can shorten a degree. Dalhousie awards it for grades of 5, 6 or 7; McGill grants up to 30 credits of advanced standing for the Diploma.

The IB Career-related Programme is treated inconsistently. Toronto does not accept it as a basis of admission at all; Dalhousie admits CP students who combine two IB courses with three Grade 12 academic courses.

Quebec bachelor's degrees are often three years rather than four because Quebec students arrive having done two years of CEGEP. An IB Diploma holder from abroad enters the university directly and takes the longer version. Confirm the programme length before accepting.
No Canadian body is known to assess the IB Diploma formally as a qualification, as a NARIC or ENIC centre would in Europe; the universities appear to be the only rule-owners.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: The whole system outside Quebec, and much of it inside. Every province except Quebec teaches primarily in English, and Quebec has three large English-language universities, two of which are on this page.
language.englishProof: Set by each university. An IB Diploma with English A is normally accepted, and UBC states a minimum of 3 in IB English A at either level for all programmes. McGill waives further proof for anyone who has lived and studied for at least four years in a country where English is the primary language, and reserves the right to ask anyway. Confirm on the university's own page.
notes: In Quebec you can study entirely in English, and daily life, part-time work and paperwork are in French. The CAQ and the provincial health rules are Quebec's, not Canada's.
French is useful and never required outside Quebec.

feeContext.summary: Canada has no EU or EEA fee category. The line is drawn at Canadian citizenship or permanent residence, so an EU/EEA student pays the full international rate everywhere, with no reciprocal arrangement of any kind.
feeContext.typicalRange: CAD 51,530 to CAD 66,678 a year at UBC in 2026/27, depending on the faculty; CAD 39,007 for a BA at Saskatchewan in 2026/27; about CAD 28,000 on average at Manitoba. Ontario is not established for any year.

feeContext.summary: The same rate, on the same basis. Fees are set by each university rather than by any province or by the federal government, so they are not comparable across the country and a figure from one university says nothing about another.
feeContext.typicalRange: Verified at UBC for 2026/27: Arts CAD 51,530.40, Science and Computer Science CAD 53,082.00, Engineering CAD 66,199.66 for a 37-credit first year, Commerce CAD 66,678.30.

livingCostMonthly.note: Derived from the federal immigration minimum of CAD 23,448 for twelve months and rounded. It is the figure you must prove to get a study permit outside Quebec, not a realistic Vancouver or Toronto budget, and it explicitly excludes tuition and travel.

livingContext.livingCostYear: CAD 23,448 for twelve months, for a single applicant outside Quebec applying on or after 1 September 2026. The previous band was CAD 22,895 and the amounts are revised annually, so a figure remembered from an older application is short. Quebec assesses financial capacity itself, through its own immigration ministry and for the CAQ, and the number is different.
livingContext.housing: Most universities guarantee first-year residence only to students who apply by a separate housing deadline, months before term and usually in spring. UBC's is 1 May 2027. Take the guarantee: Vancouver and Toronto private rentals are very expensive and finding a room from Denmark is very hard.
livingContext.healthcare: Provincial, not national, and very different from one province to the next. Ontario excludes international students from the public plan entirely and enrols them in UHIP; British Columbia, Alberta and Nova Scotia admit them on their own conditions, each after a wait; Quebec requires continuous private or public cover for the whole study stay as a condition of the CAQ. The EHIC and the Danish yellow card are not valid anywhere in Canada.
livingContext.workRights: A study permit carries work rights during study and the Post-Graduation Work Permit after it. For a bachelor's, master's or doctoral degree there is no field-of-study restriction on the PGWP, which is the restriction that applies to non-degree programmes and the clearest practical difference between a university and a college here. Apply within 180 days of confirmation that you completed the programme, and expect to show Canadian Language Benchmarks 7 in English across all four skills.
livingContext.residency: A study permit, not a visa-free stay. Since 2024 Canada caps the number of study permit applications it will process: 309,670 for 2026, allocated by province, with Ontario 104,780, Quebec 93,069, British Columbia 32,596, Alberta 32,271 and Nova Scotia 8,480. Undergraduates need a Provincial Attestation Letter to enter that queue and the university requests it after you accept the offer; master's and doctoral students at public institutions stopped needing one on 1 January 2026. No allocation beyond 2026 had been published as of September 2026, so the 2027 position is unknown rather than unchanged. In Quebec, a Certificat d'acceptation du Quebec replaces the attestation letter and must be granted before the federal permit.
funding: Entrance scholarships from the university itself, usually awarded from the admission application with no separate form. The exceptions are the large named awards, and they close early: UBC's International Scholars deadline is 15 November 2026, two months before the ordinary application, and McGill's Major Entrance Scholarship closes six days after its application.

The University of Toronto's Lester B. Pearson International Scholarships and UBC's International Scholars programmes are full-cost awards for international students. Both need school nomination in the autumn. Ask your studievejleder in September 2026.
Faculty and programme awards, especially in engineering and commerce, awarded after first year on results.

funding.note: A full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules, with its own ties-to-Denmark form: check su.dk before budgeting.

funding: There is no Canadian government grant or loan for international undergraduates. Budget on paying tuition from family funds, savings and scholarships.

jurisdictions.name: Ontario
jurisdictions.summary: The largest system, with its own central application service for universities. Applications go through the OUAC, which rations choices by charging for them, and which sets no deadline at all for an applicant from outside Ontario. Ontario also runs a second, separate central service for its 24 colleges.

variations.label: Health cover
variations.summary: The one province that excludes international students from the public plan for the whole degree. You are enrolled automatically in UHIP, a not-for-profit plan created by Ontario's universities, it is mandatory, and the premium is billed to your student account. Budget for it as a cost rather than a formality.

variations.label: What applying costs
variations.summary: CAD 159 to the OUAC for three programme choices and CAD 51 for each further one, plus a document evaluation fee charged once per university - CAD 98 at Toronto, CAD 125 at Western, CAD 95 at Queen's, Waterloo and McMaster, CAD 93 at Ottawa, CAD 90 at York and Toronto Metropolitan, CAD 85 at Carleton, CAD 95 at Guelph. A second programme at the same university is cheap; a fourth university is not.

variations.label: Deadlines
variations.summary: The OUAC sets none for an international applicant and says so: deadlines belong to the university and sometimes to the programme. Toronto's is 15 January 2027, with documents by 1 February and an early round for applications in by 7 November 2026. The other Ontario universities set their own dates; read them on each university's page.

variations.label: Study permit queue
variations.summary: 104,780 study permit application spaces in 2026, the largest provincial allocation in the country. The attestation letter comes from the institution whose offer you have accepted, and the province distributes its allocation among its own institutions.

jurisdictions.name: British Columbia
jurisdictions.summary: One application account covering all 25 public institutions, universities and colleges together, with no limit on choices and nothing charged by the platform. What it does not give you is a shared deadline or a shared fee: both belong to the institution, and the three universities here disagree on both.

variations.label: Health cover
variations.summary: Compulsory enrolment in the provincial Medical Services Plan for a study permit of six months or more, with a health fee invoiced. Cover starts only after the balance of your arrival month plus two more, so arriving in late August means no provincial cover until 1 November and private insurance until then.

variations.label: What applying costs
variations.summary: Nothing to EducationPlannerBC and the institution's own fee to the institution: CAD 130 at Simon Fraser for an international applicant, CAD 184.00 at Victoria where any transcript comes from outside Canada. CAD 173.25 at UBC for an applicant on a study permit. Adding another choice costs only that institution's fee.

variations.label: Deadlines
variations.summary: Set by each institution, and the platform states that plainly. UBC closes 15 January 2027 at 23:59 Pacific, Simon Fraser 31 January 2027, and Victoria publishes its dates on each programme page instead. UBC's International Scholars award closes on 15 November 2026, two months ahead of everything else.

variations.label: Tuition
variations.summary: Published ahead of time: UBC's 2026/27 international undergraduate rates run from CAD 51,530.40 for Arts to CAD 66,678.30 for Commerce, and UBC caps the annual rise at 3% for four years for a student starting in 2026/27.

jurisdictions.name: Quebec
jurisdictions.summary: No shared application service and a second immigration system. You apply to each university directly, and before the federal study permit you need a Certificat d'acceptation du Quebec with its own fee, its own financial test and its own processing time. Quebec is also the province with a whole extra level of education, the CEGEP, between school and university.

variations.label: Immigration
variations.summary: A Certificat d'acceptation du Quebec is required in addition to the federal study permit and has to be granted first. Quebec assesses your financial capacity itself rather than applying the federal CAD 23,448 figure. This is why Concordia asks international applicants to apply a month before its own deadline.

variations.label: Health cover
variations.summary: Continuous health and hospitalisation insurance for the entire study stay is a condition of the CAQ, not merely a requirement on arrival. Whether you can instead join the Quebec public plan depends on any social security agreement between Quebec and the country where you are insured or hold citizenship, and is not confirmed here; ask the RAMQ or your university.

variations.label: Deadlines
variations.summary: McGill closes on 15 January 2027 for anyone last studying at a high school outside Canada, with documents by 1 March and its Major Entrance Scholarship by 21 January. Concordia closes on 1 March and asks international applicants for 1 February. Two universities, two miles apart, six weeks apart.

jurisdictions.name: Alberta
jurisdictions.summary: No shared application service. You apply to each university directly, and at the University of Alberta the deadline is set per programme rather than per institution, behind a faculty-and-term filter, so there is no one Alberta date to know.

variations.label: Health cover
variations.summary: An international student with a twelve-month study permit valid for an Alberta institution, intending to live in Alberta for twelve months or more, may apply for the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan. Enrolment has to be reconfirmed every year by 30 November, and missing that interrupts cover.

variations.label: Deadlines
variations.summary: Published per programme for Fall 2027 and not institution-wide. The minimum admission average also varies by faculty and changes every year, so there is no single number to aim at either. Read both off the programme you actually want.

variations.label: What applying costs
variations.summary: CAD 150 at the University of Alberta for a new applicant, paid to the university. The University of Calgary's fee was not established.

jurisdictions.name: Nova Scotia
jurisdictions.summary: No shared application service, and the smallest study permit allocation of the five provinces here. Dalhousie sets dated deadlines only for its competitive health programmes and considers applications to everything else up to the start of classes where space remains.

variations.label: Health cover
variations.summary: An international student holding a study permit valid for twelve months or more may be eligible for the provincial health insurance programme. A waiting period applies on arrival from outside the province and the page does not say how long it is, which is the number you would actually need.

variations.label: Deadlines
variations.summary: For September 2027 entry Dalhousie closes Nursing, Health Sciences, Medical Sciences and Social Work on 15 February 2027 and Architecture on 1 March 2027, and considers everything else where space remains until classes start. The scholarship deadline is also 15 February 2027, and offers and awards must be accepted by 1 May 2027. Guaranteed residence needs an application by 15 May 2027.

variations.label: Study permit queue
variations.summary: 8,480 study permit application spaces in 2026, against Ontario's 104,780. The queue is smaller because the province is, not because it is easier, and the allocation is divided among Nova Scotia's own institutions.

jurisdictions.name: Manitoba
jurisdictions.summary: No shared application service: you apply to the University of Manitoba on its own application. It asks for 24 IB points, and its average first-year international tuition and fees are about CAD 28,000.

variations.label: Study permit queue
variations.summary: 11,196 study permit application spaces in 2026, divided among Manitoba's own institutions. The attestation letter comes from the institution whose offer you accept.

variations.label: Tuition
variations.summary: The University of Manitoba gives about CAD 28,000 as the average first-year tuition and fees for an international student, roughly half of UBC's lowest faculty rate.

jurisdictions.name: Saskatchewan
jurisdictions.summary: No shared application service: you apply to the University of Saskatchewan directly. It reads an IB total out of 45 and converts it to a percentage for its admission average.

variations.label: Study permit queue
variations.summary: 11,349 study permit application spaces in 2026, divided among Saskatchewan's own institutions.

variations.label: Tuition
variations.summary: A full-load BA costs an international student CAD 39,007 in 2026/27, charged per course rather than as a flat annual fee.

sectorLandscape.summary: Canada divides post-secondary education twice over, and English-language advice usually describes only one half of one division. The first division is the university and the college: four-year degrees against one-to-three-year diplomas, applied through different services even inside the same province, and carrying different post-study work rights. The second is Quebec, which puts a whole extra level between school and university - the CEGEP, two years before a Quebec student even reaches a bachelor's, which is why Quebec degrees are often three years rather than four.

routes.what: The four-year bachelor's degree, awarded by provincially chartered universities. This is what every English-language guide to Canada is describing and what all twenty institutions on this page are. Several build paid work terms into the degree as co-op, which is a Canadian speciality rather than a national rule. A degree also carries the Post-Graduation Work Permit without the field-of-study restriction that applies to shorter programmes, which is a major practical difference between this route and the next one.
routes.note: In Quebec a bachelor's is often three years, because a Quebec student has already spent two years at CEGEP. An IB Diploma holder arriving from abroad takes the longer version. Confirm the length before accepting an offer.

routes.what: Certificates, diplomas, apprenticeships and some degrees, taught for a named occupation rather than a discipline. Ontario alone has 24 of them, and they are applied for through ontariocolleges.ca rather than the OUAC - a different central service for a different sector in the same province. Admission is stated in terms of an Ontario high school diploma, and what that means for an IB Diploma holder from abroad is not published; Ontario's answer is to contact a college directly.
routes.note: Listed because it exists and is easy to overlook. Two cautions: no college is covered institution by institution on this page, and the Post-Graduation Work Permit rules for non-degree programmes are tighter than for a degree, which is a consequence worth understanding before choosing this route.

routes.localName: polytechnic / institute of technology and advanced learning
routes.what: A name rather than a category. Ontario's own list of its 24 public colleges includes Seneca Polytechnic and two institutions styled Institute of Technology and Advanced Learning alongside the colleges of applied arts and technology, which means a student reading a Canadian polytechnic's website is reading a college's. The name signals a stronger applied-technology and degree-granting emphasis, not a separate legal sector.
routes.note: Named here so that a student who meets the word knows where it sits. Whether they differ from the other colleges in anything a student would notice is not covered here.

routes.what: Quebec's own level between school and university, with no equivalent anywhere else in Canada: 48 public CEGEPs, five of them English-language, plus about 70 private colleges. Two programmes lead to a Diploma of College Studies. The pre-university programme takes two years and is the normal Quebec route into a bachelor's degree. The technical programme takes three years, includes at least one workplace placement, and is built to end in a job rather than in a degree. The public network admits international students through the Federation des cegeps to around 125 programmes.
routes.note: It is rarely mentioned to students from abroad, and it is the reason Quebec degrees look short. What it would mean for an IB Diploma holder is not known: whether a full Diploma is treated as over-qualification for a pre-university DEC, and whether a technical DEC would admit one, are open questions to put to the Fédération des cégeps.

notes: Written after the routes, the Evidence and the jurisdictions, because writing it is the act of publishing and the floor holds it from that moment.

Seven jurisdictions are declared because seven have institutions in this record. Canada has thirteen provinces and territories and the other six have not been looked at; their absence here is a gap in coverage, not a finding that they lack universities.

Three routes cover the seven: the OUAC for Ontario, EducationPlannerBC for British Columbia, and one apply-direct route shared by Quebec, Alberta, Nova Scotia, Manitoba and Saskatchewan, which lists those five jurisdictions by name.

Institution-level dates were read in full only for Toronto, UBC, Simon Fraser, McGill, Concordia and Dalhousie. Waterloo, Queen's, McMaster, Western, Ottawa, Alberta, Calgary and Victoria sit on a recorded route with no date of their own established.

Re-check in autumn 2026: the 2027 study permit cap and provincial allocations, which had not been published; and any Ontario university's 2027/28 tuition, which Toronto says is not set until the spring.

Not established: whether a student from Denmark or elsewhere in the EU/EEA qualifies for the Quebec public health plan under a social security agreement, because the RAMQ pages are behind a bot-protection challenge; the length of Nova Scotia's health-cover waiting period; and what any Canadian college or CEGEP requires of an IB Diploma holder.
Programme-level records not yet created. Stages 1 to 5 of the research brief are done for the six institutions named above; stage 6 is not done for any.

2026-09-24 audit: York, Toronto Metropolitan, Carleton and Guelph (Ontario, OUAC), Manitoba and Saskatchewan (new jurisdictions, applying directly) added from the IB transcript counts in docs/research/IB_DISCOVERY.md. Their own dates were not read.
